taxonomy.name: The Data Center Stack Industry Taxonomy
taxonomy.purpose: Classify organizations and industries by the data-center function they directly perform.

classification_rules.primary_industry: Select the industry that best represents the organization's principal data-center function.
classification_rules.primary_layer: Use the layer assigned to the primary industry.
classification_rules.secondary_industries: Assign only when the organization directly performs another material function.
classification_rules.do_not_overmap: Do not assign a layer merely because an organization sells to, buys from, or is used by that layer.
classification_rules.specialties: Use specialties to add precision without creating unnecessary industries.
classification_rules.stack_consumer: Organizations that primarily consume data-center infrastructure but do not supply a Stack function should be classified as Stack Consumers.
classification_rules.ecosystem_enabler: Organizations that advise, finance, insure, regulate, educate, research, recruit for, or convene the ecosystem should be classified outside Layers 1-6.
classification_rules.uncertain: Use Research Required when evidence is insufficient instead of guessing.

layers.name: Foundation
layers.definition: Land, power, water, structure and the physical facility everything else depends on.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.definition: The physical and digital building blocks: compute, storage, network, power, cooling, connectivity, security and software.

layers.name: Deployment
layers.definition: Deploy, integrate, migrate, upgrade, relocate and retire infrastructure across its lifecycle.

layers.name: Operations
layers.definition: Monitor, secure, maintain and optimize production infrastructure for reliability and uptime.

layers.name: Platform
layers.definition: Turn physical infrastructure into consumable capacity through virtualization, orchestration and cloud services.

layers.name: Workloads
layers.definition: Applications, services and digital workloads that consume platform and infrastructure capacity.

industries.name: Data Center Developers
industries.definition: Organizations that originate, entitle, finance and develop data center facilities or campuses.

industries.name: Site Selection & Data Center Real Estate
industries.definition: Organizations focused on locating, acquiring, leasing, brokering or advising on land and real estate for data center development or occupancy.
excludes: general commercial brokerage with no data center practice

industries.name: Electric Utilities & Grid Providers
industries.definition: Organizations providing grid interconnection, transmission or distribution of electricity to data center sites.

industries.name: Power Generation & Energy Supply
industries.definition: Organizations developing or supplying utility-scale electrical generation or contracted energy used to serve data center demand.
excludes: backup generators installed at data centers

industries.name: Water & Utility Infrastructure
industries.definition: Organizations providing water, wastewater or related municipal utility infrastructure needed to support data center sites.

industries.name: Architecture & Engineering
industries.definition: Firms providing multidisciplinary architecture, civil, structural and facility engineering for data center buildings and campuses.

industries.name: MEP Engineering
industries.definition: Engineering firms primarily responsible for mechanical, electrical and plumbing system design in data center facilities.

industries.name: General Contractors & Construction Managers
industries.definition: Organizations responsible for overall construction execution, subcontractor coordination, schedule and delivery of data center facilities.

industries.name: Civil & Site Contractors
industries.definition: Contractors performing grading, excavation, underground utilities, roads, drainage and other site preparation work.

industries.name: Electrical Contractors
industries.definition: Contractors installing facility electrical systems such as switchgear, busway, feeders, grounding and medium-voltage distribution.

industries.name: Mechanical Contractors
industries.definition: Contractors installing cooling plants, HVAC, piping and other facility mechanical systems.

industries.name: Facility Commissioning & Integrated Systems Testing
industries.definition: Organizations verifying that facility systems are installed, integrated and performing as intended before or during turnover to operations.

industries.name: Server & Compute Hardware
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of server systems and general-purpose compute hardware installed in data centers.

industries.name: Storage Hardware
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of physical data storage systems and appliances.

industries.name: Semiconductors & Accelerators
industries.definition: Manufacturers of CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators and other silicon providing data center compute capability.

industries.name: Network Equipment
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of switches, routers and active network infrastructure used inside data centers.

industries.name: Optical Transceivers & Photonics
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of optical modules, transceivers and photonic components used for high-speed data center connectivity.

industries.name: Fiber, Copper & Passive Connectivity Products
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of passive fiber, copper, connectors, patching and cable-management systems.

industries.name: Carriers, Fiber & Interconnection Providers
industries.definition: Organizations providing telecommunications transport, dark fiber, wavelengths, internet transit, cross-connect or interconnection services.

industries.name: Critical Power Infrastructure
industries.definition: Manufacturers of systems that condition, protect or maintain continuous electrical power to critical data center loads.

industries.name: Electrical Distribution Equipment
industries.definition: Manufacturers of transformers, switchgear, busway, PDUs, RPPs and related electrical distribution equipment.

industries.name: Backup Generation
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of standby or emergency generation systems used at data center facilities.

industries.name: Fuel Cells & On-Site Energy Systems
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of fuel cells and other on-site primary or supplemental energy systems deployed at data centers.

industries.name: Air Cooling & Thermal Management
industries.definition: Manufacturers of chillers, CRAHs, CRACs, heat exchangers and other air-based data center cooling systems.

industries.name: Liquid Cooling Infrastructure
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of direct-to-chip, immersion and supporting liquid-cooling infrastructure.

industries.name: Racks, Enclosures & Containment
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of racks, cabinets, cages and containment systems used to house IT infrastructure.

industries.name: Raised Floor, Ceiling & White-Space Systems
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of modular physical systems used to organize and support the data center white space.

industries.name: Physical Security Infrastructure
industries.definition: Manufacturers and suppliers of access control, surveillance, biometrics and physical security systems.

industries.name: BMS, EPMS & Facility Controls
industries.definition: Technology providers supplying building, electrical power and facility control systems used to monitor and control physical infrastructure.
excludes: DCIM focused primarily on IT assets

industries.name: DCIM & Infrastructure Management Software
industries.definition: Software providers whose products inventory, model, monitor or manage data center physical and IT infrastructure, capacity and environmental state.

industries.name: Data Center Logistics
industries.definition: Organizations coordinating the movement, staging, delivery, tracking and lifecycle logistics of data center infrastructure.
excludes: general freight with no data center specialization

industries.name: Warehousing & Staging
industries.definition: Organizations providing secure storage, receiving, inventory, staging, kitting and pre-deployment preparation.

industries.name: Specialized Transportation & Freight
industries.definition: Transportation providers specializing in secure, time-sensitive or high-value movement of data center infrastructure.

industries.name: Rigging & Heavy Equipment Moving
industries.definition: Organizations that lift, position and move heavy infrastructure such as generators, transformers, switchgear and chillers.

industries.name: Freight Forwarding & International Logistics
industries.definition: Organizations coordinating international transportation, customs, documentation and multimodal movement of data center equipment.

industries.name: Systems Integration
industries.definition: Organizations combining hardware, software, network and infrastructure components into functioning data center systems.

industries.name: Network Integration & Turn-Up
industries.definition: Organizations implementing, configuring, testing and turning up network infrastructure inside data centers.

industries.name: Rack & Stack / Equipment Installation
industries.definition: Service providers physically installing, racking, cabling and preparing servers, storage, network and related IT equipment for service.

industries.name: Structured Cabling Installation
industries.definition: Contractors installing, terminating, testing and documenting copper and fiber structured cabling.

industries.name: White-Space Buildout & Fit-Out
industries.definition: Organizations completing deployable data hall or customer white-space fit-outs after the base facility is available.

industries.name: Data Center Migration & Relocation
industries.definition: Organizations planning and executing physical relocation of production infrastructure between rooms, buildings, campuses or data centers.
excludes: logical cloud migration with no physical move

industries.name: ITAD & Asset Disposition
industries.definition: Organizations processing retired IT assets through data destruction, remarketing, recycling and disposition.

industries.name: Data Center Decommissioning
industries.definition: Organizations physically removing infrastructure and restoring space during data center exits, consolidations or retirements.
excludes: ITAD processing when disposition is the primary service

industries.name: Deployment Project Management & Coordination
industries.definition: Organizations whose primary role is coordinating multi-vendor infrastructure deployment programs, schedules, sites and implementation activities.
excludes: advisory consulting with no execution responsibility

industries.name: Retail Colocation Operators
industries.definition: Operators providing smaller-scale colocation space, power, connectivity and support directly to enterprise and network customers.

industries.name: Wholesale & Hyperscale Data Center Operators
industries.definition: Operators providing large-scale suites, halls or dedicated facilities to hyperscale, cloud and large enterprise customers.
excludes: developer-only companies that do not operate

industries.name: Edge Data Center Operators
industries.definition: Operators of smaller distributed facilities positioned closer to end users, networks or localized demand.

industries.name: Critical Environment Operations
industries.definition: Providers responsible for day-to-day operation of critical electrical and mechanical facility infrastructure.

industries.name: Facility Management Services
industries.definition: Organizations managing the broader operational, maintenance, vendor and service functions of active data center facilities.

industries.name: Energy, Capacity & Efficiency Optimization
industries.definition: Organizations providing ongoing optimization of power, cooling, capacity and energy performance in operating data centers.

industries.name: Smart Hands & Remote Hands
industries.definition: Providers performing on-demand physical technical tasks inside operating data centers for remote customers.

industries.name: Network Operations & NOC Services
industries.definition: Providers continuously monitoring and operating customer networks and coordinating incident response.

industries.name: Managed Compute Services
industries.definition: Providers administering servers, operating systems and compute infrastructure as an ongoing service.

industries.name: Managed Network Services
industries.definition: Providers administering switching, routing, firewalls and network infrastructure on an ongoing basis.

industries.name: Managed Storage & Data Protection Services
industries.definition: Providers administering storage, backup, replication and infrastructure-level data protection systems.

industries.name: OEM Infrastructure Maintenance
industries.definition: Equipment manufacturers providing recurring field service, preventive maintenance and lifecycle support for installed infrastructure.

industries.name: Third-Party Infrastructure Maintenance
industries.definition: Independent service providers maintaining installed IT, power, cooling or network infrastructure across multiple manufacturers.

industries.name: Asset & Inventory Operations
industries.definition: Service providers maintaining operational asset records, rack inventory, chain of custody and lifecycle status in active data centers.

industries.name: Public Cloud Infrastructure
industries.definition: Providers delivering elastic compute, storage, networking and related infrastructure through shared public cloud platforms.

industries.name: Private Cloud Platforms
industries.definition: Platforms and providers enabling cloud-like infrastructure services within dedicated private environments.

industries.name: Sovereign & Regulated Cloud
industries.definition: Cloud providers designed around jurisdictional, regulatory, data residency or national sovereignty requirements.
excludes: general public cloud without sovereignty controls

industries.name: AI / GPU Cloud
industries.definition: Providers delivering accelerated GPU or AI infrastructure capacity as a cloud service.

industries.name: Bare Metal Infrastructure Services
industries.definition: Providers delivering dedicated physical servers as rapidly consumable infrastructure services.

industries.name: Managed Hosting
industries.definition: Providers delivering hosted infrastructure together with operational management and support.

industries.name: Compute Virtualization Platforms
industries.definition: Software platforms abstracting physical compute systems into virtual machines and virtual compute pools.

industries.name: Software-Defined Networking & Network Virtualization
industries.definition: Platforms abstracting and programmatically controlling network services independently of physical network hardware.

industries.name: Software-Defined Storage
industries.definition: Platforms abstracting physical storage resources into software-controlled storage pools and services.

industries.name: Container Platforms & Kubernetes
industries.definition: Platforms providing container runtime, cluster management and application infrastructure built around containers.

industries.name: Infrastructure Automation & IaC
industries.definition: Platforms automating infrastructure provisioning, configuration and lifecycle using code and declarative workflows.

industries.name: Hybrid & Multi-Cloud Management
industries.definition: Platforms managing policy, provisioning, visibility and operations across multiple private and public cloud environments.

industries.name: Edge Computing Platforms
industries.definition: Platforms distributing compute and application execution closer to users, devices or localized data sources.

industries.name: CDN & Content Delivery Infrastructure
industries.definition: Platforms distributing and caching digital content across geographically distributed infrastructure for performance and resilience.

industries.name: Foundation Model Providers
industries.definition: Organizations developing and operating large general-purpose AI models as a primary digital product or service.

industries.name: AI Applications & Agents
industries.definition: Providers of end-user or enterprise applications whose primary functionality is powered by AI models or autonomous agents.

industries.name: AI Inference Services
industries.definition: Providers delivering production-scale model inference, serving or AI execution as a specialized service.

industries.name: HPC & Scientific Computing
industries.definition: Organizations operating compute-intensive scientific, engineering, simulation or research workloads.

industries.name: Enterprise SaaS
industries.definition: Providers of general enterprise software applications delivered as digital services.

industries.name: Collaboration & Productivity Platforms
industries.definition: Providers of messaging, collaboration, office productivity and workplace communication applications.

industries.name: Database & Data Platforms
industries.definition: Providers whose primary service is database, data warehouse, data lake or managed data platform functionality.

industries.name: Analytics & Business Intelligence Platforms
industries.definition: Providers of large-scale analytics, visualization and business intelligence applications.

industries.name: Cybersecurity Platforms
industries.definition: Providers of digital security applications and services protecting identities, endpoints, networks, applications or data.

industries.name: Streaming Media Platforms
industries.definition: Providers delivering large-scale video, audio or live-streaming services to consumers or enterprises.

industries.name: Online Gaming Platforms
industries.definition: Providers operating online multiplayer, cloud gaming or game-service workloads at scale.

industries.name: Social & Community Platforms
industries.definition: Providers operating large-scale social networks, communities, messaging or user-generated content platforms.

industries.name: E-Commerce & Marketplace Platforms
industries.definition: Providers operating large-scale digital commerce, marketplace or retail transaction platforms.

industries.name: Payments & Transaction Processing
industries.definition: Providers operating digital payment, settlement or high-volume financial transaction processing platforms.

industries.name: Electronic Trading & Market Platforms
industries.definition: Providers operating electronic exchanges, trading systems, market data or latency-sensitive financial platforms.

industries.name: Industry-Specific Digital Platforms
industries.definition: Providers operating large-scale digital platforms tailored to sectors such as healthcare, telecommunications, transportation, education or government.
excludes: ordinary enterprises merely consuming IT infrastructure

ecosystem_enablers.name: Consulting & Advisory
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations providing strategic, operational or technical advisory services to data center market participants.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Investment, Finance & Capital
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations financing, investing in or underwriting data center projects, companies or infrastructure.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Insurance & Risk
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations providing insurance, brokerage and risk-transfer services to the data center ecosystem.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Legal Services
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Law firms and legal service providers supporting data center transactions, development, operations or regulation.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Recruiting & Workforce
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations supplying recruiting, staffing or workforce services to data center companies.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Education & Training
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations providing professional training, curriculum or workforce development for data center roles.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Certification & Accreditation
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations issuing professional, facility or technical certifications and accreditations.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Standards & Research
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations producing technical standards, research, benchmarks or industry guidance.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Trade Associations
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Membership organizations representing data center, technology, energy or infrastructure participants.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Media & Publishing
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations reporting on, analyzing or publishing information about the data center industry.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Events & Conferences
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations producing data center conferences, summits, exhibitions or professional gatherings.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Government & Economic Development
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Government agencies and economic development organizations supporting, regulating or attracting data center activity.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Environmental & Sustainability Advisory
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations advising on environmental impact, sustainability, carbon, water or reporting requirements.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Security Guard & Protective Services
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations providing human physical-security and protective services at data center facilities.

ecosystem_enablers.name: Procurement & Sourcing Advisory
ecosystem_enablers.definition: Organizations providing sourcing, procurement, vendor management or supply-chain advisory services without directly supplying Stack infrastructure.
